newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine premier sees foreign bond issue in May.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine premier sees foreign bond issue in May.

text.p: Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko told parliament on Tuesday that Ukraine would issue its first foreign bonds in early May.
"We will issue foreign bonds between May 1 and 5," Lazarenko said in response to a deputy's question after a speech on the former Soviet republic's troubled economy.
"In terms of entering the European market -- Eurobonds and Samurai bonds -- I think the first step is completed and we will have the necessary resources by May," he said during his speech.
A deputy finance minister said last month that Ukraine was still researching the issue and had not yet selected an agency to conduct a rating, or where to launch the first bond.
The government had said it was planning to issue $250 million worth of foreign bonds in the first quarter.
Local media, quoting unnamed sources, have said Nomura Securities Company Ltd would lead the issue, but there has been no official announcement on the subject.
